songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Adventurous second set with The Other One jam and tight drumming
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a solid acoustic first set that segues into an exploratory second set highlighted by the Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One sequence and a high‑energy Good Lovin' jam. Jerry’s guitar tone shines despite some vocal strain, and the drum duo provides standout interludes.
ai_show_review.review: June 7, 1970 at Fillmore West finds the Dead in a transitional phase – an acoustic‑heavy first set that eases the crowd into a free‑form, jam‑laden second half. Highlights include a seamless Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One → Cryptical reprise suite that showcases Mickey and Billy’s dynamic lock‑in, as well as a soaring Good Lovin' > Drums > Good Lovin' stretch that feels both tight and exploratory. Jerry Garcia delivers his trademark fluid guitar work throughout; his vocals on New Speedway Boogie sound a little strained to some ears but the pedal‑steel flourishes keep the momentum high. Phil’s bass underpins the improvisations, though one listener noted a few off‑key harmonies. Bob Weir steps forward for lead vocals on Cosmic Charlie and adds a friendly “Peace, Bob” sign‑off. The recording quality varies – the Hollister soundboard capture (gd70-06-07.sbd.hollister.98.sbeok.shnf) offers generally clear audio with occasional low‑end heaviness, while the Clevenger board is crisp and the audience FLAC is crystal‑clear but lacks some instrument definition. Overall, the performance is a compelling snapshot of the Dead’s evolving sound in 1970.

best_recording.reason: Provides a full soundboard capture of both acoustic and electric sets with decent clarity; includes the standout jams while being the most complete version available.

key_highlights: Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One suite showcases tight improvisation and dynamic drumming.
Good Lovin' > Drums > Good Lovin' jam adds high‑energy momentum to the second set.
Strong acoustic selections – Cumberland Blues, New Speedway Boogie, and Casey Jones – set a relaxed yet adventurous tone.
Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann’s interludes receive particular praise for texture and drive.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is praised throughout, especially in the The Other One jam; his vocals on New Speedway Boogie are noted as mixed/strained by some listeners.
band_performance.Phil: Phil provides a solid bass foundation; one reviewer mentioned a few off‑key harmonies but no major issues.
band_performance.Bob: Bob takes lead vocals on Cosmic Charlie and adds a friendly sign‑off, contributing to the set’s character.
band_performance.Mickey: Mickey delivers nuanced drum interludes, notably the quiet build before The Other One and the textured segment in Good Lovin'.
band_performance.Billy: Billy locks in with Mickey on the high‑energy drumming sections, driving the crowd during the jam-heavy moments.
